name: Veeva Systems
thesis: Vertical life-sciences SaaS with a regulatory moat. Two engines: (1) R&D + Quality (Development Cloud / Vault) is the durable compounder - sticky, GxP-validated workflow software for clinical trials and quality, now the LARGER segment (R&D subscription > Commercial); (2) Vault CRM migration off Salesforce (2025-29) is medium-term OPTIONALITY, not yet a confirmed uptick. The classic vertical-SaaS bet: best-in-class gross retention + multi-product cross-sell driving NDR and capital efficiency, at ~15% growth with non-GAAP operating margin >40%. IMPORTANT: Veeva does not disclose NDR - it must be proxied (subscription revenue / customer count). The CRM leg is the swing factor and is contested: Salesforce Life Sciences Cloud has signed 40+ life-sci customers (incl. a top-3 pharma defection); the real scoreboard is Vault CRM live-customer count and top-20 commitments, not management adjectives.
key_driver: R&D/Development Cloud growth + Vault CRM migration scoreboard (live-customer count, top-20 commitments)

tier_1_kpis.break_condition: R&D/Development Cloud growth <10% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (the durable compounder stalls)

tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Implied NDR trends below ~110% (cross-sell engine weakening)

competitive_watchlist: Salesforce (Life Sciences Cloud - now an active CRM competitor)
thesis_breakers_qualitative: A top-20 pharma publicly defects/churns from Vault CRM to Salesforce
Net-new CRM deals consistently lost to Salesforce Life Sciences Cloud

nuance.bear_case: CRM is the single biggest unresolved risk. Salesforce Life Sciences Cloud signed 40+ life-sci customers by Dec 2025 including a top-3 global pharma defection (Takeda, Pfizer named); IQVIA's OCE is migrating to Salesforce's stack; 6 of the top-20 remain undecided. FY27 subscription guide decelerates to ~13% with explicitly NO AI revenue offset, and multiple banks cut targets on multiple compression. The 'CRM uptick improving' claim is not yet visible in reported revenue (legacy + Vault CRM are blended).
nuance.adversarial_take: 'NDR improving' is faith-based - Veeva never discloses it. Implied NDR (rev / customers) looks flat-to-slightly-down as Commercial matures. The moat (GxP switching costs, R&D > Commercial) is real and margins are elite (44.9% non-GAAP), so the durable-compounder leg holds even if CRM disappoints - but ~21x fwd P/E is pricing a re-acceleration the 13% guide doesn't support.
nuance.stress_test: A top-20 defection to Salesforce + subscription growth printing <13% for 2 Qs would move this from Watch to Broken.

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters - outright top-line contraction.
FCF margin below 5% for 2 consecutive Qs - cash conversion broken. (Universal floor; per-ticker rules below are stricter.)
Operating cash flow declining >10% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs.

break_rules_soft.name: subscription_decel_2q
break_rules_soft.evidence_template: Revenue YoY decel {first_bps}->{second_bps}bps over {periods}Q (FY27 sub guide ~13% vs 17% FY26)

business_model_rules.narrative: Total revenue YoY < 12% for 2Q - base case for compounding vertical-SaaS; sub-12 means the durable-growth thesis breaks.
Subscription revenue YoY < 12% for 2Q - the high-quality compounding stream stalls (FY27 guide ~13% sits just above this).
R&D/Development Cloud YoY < 10% for 2Q - the durable compounder (now the larger segment) fails. Relaxed from 15 to capture sentiment, not a hard 15% line.
Non-GAAP op margin < 38% for 2Q - VEEV's structural floor is ~40-45%; SBC-adjusted profitability is the right metric vs GAAP.
